To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PTPL1 is decreased in breast tumors compared with nonmalingant tissues; in breast cancer cell lines, PTPL1 inhibition enhances tumor growth in athmic mice and also enhances cell proliferation and invasion, and these effects are mediated by the inhibition of Src activity.
PTPL1, a tumor suppressor, regulates breast cancer cell growth by directly dephosphorylating and inhibiting the kinase Src.
PTPL1, a protein tyrosine phosphate, is able to inhibit the activity of the oncogene Src in breast cancer cells, thus reducing their aggressiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PTPL1 in breast cancer and the mechanisms involved.
the identification of PTPLI as the first phosphoprotein phosphatase capable of directly inhibiting Src activity in cells.
the identification and functional characterization of a new tumor suppressor, which is down-regulated during tumor progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PTPL1 is a tumor suppressor that regulates cell growth through the inhibition of Src.
PTPL1 is an important tumor suppressor gene that inhibits breast tumor growth and aggressiveness by dephosphorylating and inhibiting the activity of the oncogenic kinase Src.
PTPL1 is a tumor suppressor protein tyrosine phosphate with a role in the regulation of breast cancer cell proliferation, migration, and metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PTPL1, a phosphatase that is decreased or mutated in some cancers, inhibits tumor growth and metastasis through direct dephosohorylation of Src kinase.
the PTPL1/PP2A complex dephosphorylates and inactivates the Src kinase, which is a critical regulator of cell growth and invasion in breast cancer.
PTPL1 is a tumor suppressor that regulates Src activity through direct dephosporylation of its catalytic site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein tyrosine phosphate PTPL1/ PTPN13, which is frequently inactivated in breast cancer, is a tumor suppressor that inhibits tumor aggressiveness by direct inactivation of the kinase Src.
we identify PTPL1/ PTPN13 as a tumor suppressive gene that acts by direct dephosphosphorylation of the oncogenic Src kinase.
PTPL1 is a tumor suppressor in breast cancer.
